html:
The Kalinago Territory on the east coast of Dominica was set aside by the British in 1903 as a reserve for the Kalinago, the people Europeans called Caribs. About three thousand Kalinago live there today.

Dominica's steep, wet mountains let the Kalinago hold out longer than on any other island. In 1660 France and England agreed to leave Dominica and St Vincent to them, though settlers kept coming, and Britain took the island in 1763.

The land is held in common and run by an elected chief and council. The Kalinago still make canoes and baskets in the old way. The territory is a link to the peoples who met Columbus and lived through the wars of conquest.
